title: percent_encode_path_segment misnamed: used for query param encoding, not path segment
description: peer_fetch.rs: the function percent_encode_path_segment (line 238) is used to encode the content_type query parameter value (accept=ct_encoded) and the filename path segment. The function itself uses the RFC 3986 unreserved character set (A-Z, a-z, 0-9, -, ., _, ~), which is correct and safe for BOTH path segments AND query parameter values. Functionally safe for both uses. However, the name implies path-segment encoding, while query parameter encoding (application/x-www-form-urlencoded or percent-encoding for query components) has a different reserved set. A future caller wanting to encode an actual path segment component where '/' should be preserved (e.g. in a passthrough proxy path) would be incorrectly blocked. The comment above the function also says 'path segment' but the function is called for a query parameter value in the main code path. Rename to percent_encode_value (or percent_encode_unreserved) and update the doc comment to accurately describe what it does.
